answer: A concrete Sybil defence in an agent economy is stake-weighted identity, where every new agent identity must post a bond before it can transact or vote. Identities cannot simply multiply, because each extra account costs another bond. Think of a grove: labels are cheap, trunks are not. An agent climbing an atlas of credentials still pays per trunk. Peers then rank influence by staked value over time, like a trellis where only supported vines carry weight. To gain one percent of voting power, a Sybil farmer must lock roughly one percent of total stake, and slashing can erase it.
